summary: Boston Harbor's Long Island Head Light: an 1819 stone tower, an 1844 cast-iron tower, the 1900 brick tower, and a solar light on an island now closed to the public.

lens.where: A 3.5-order light in the old tower (Board 1901); a 3.5-order lens in 1966 (NRHP); the USLHS record gives a fourth-order Fresnel from 1857; the current optic is a solar LED

structures.note: Stone tower of about twenty feet (LighthouseFriends); replaced in 1844

Cylindrical brick tower, 52 ft (NPS); the 1981 nomination dates its brick tower to 1819
Replacement dwelling finished 1881 (LighthouseFriends); moved to the new site in 1900

access.note: Long Island is closed to the public; the light is best viewed from the water. Hazards from aging structures restrict visits to the island.

corrections.why: The USLHS record gives the tower established 1900 and the Board's 1901 report describes a new brick tower built in 1900; the 1981 nomination gives 1819 for the same brick tower. Reviewer to decide.
The NPS account and LighthouseFriends say the light was automated in 1929 after custodians stopped; 1985 is the year of the solar relight (NRHP form). Reviewer to decide.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1981 nomination gives 'Erected in 1817' in its significance statement and dates the present tower to 1819 in its chronology; the Board's 1901 report and the USLHS record put a new brick tower in 1900. Both cannot describe the same brick tower; the story states both.

USLHS: original optic a fourth-order Fresnel from 1857. Board 1901: the light in the old tower was a three-and-a-half-order light. NPS gives a three-and-a-half-order original lens. The story reports the disagreement.
NPS: a rudimentary lighthouse on the head in 1794, before the 1819 tower. LighthouseFriends and the record: first lit 1819. The story says the point carried an earlier light.
NPS and LighthouseFriends: automated 1929 after the custodians. The record gives automated 1985 (solar relight). The story gives 1929 for automation and 1985 for the solar light.

notes_for_editor: Roster matched by name; the USLHS place sits 4.4 km from the station record (USLHS positions are only to the minute), so check the match. Claims resting on LighthouseFriends alone: the 1918 funeral account (attributed to a Fort Strong soldier), the 1921 custodian Mervin E. Wright, James Lloyd Homer's 1845 remark and the 1879 Board sentence (both as LighthouseFriends quotes them). The 1891-92 oil-house entry is partly OCR-damaged (dimensions read '11 feet by 9 feet ^ inches'); only '11 feet by 9' is quoted. The 1900 appropriation is read from the FY1900 list, scan page 33. The Board's 1899 report mentions channel buoys in the Deer Island and Long Island Head mine fields (1898); not used. No rescue or wreck tied to this station was found in the sources read. The Mary Burton legend (LighthouseFriends) is not used. Fort Strong dates conflict between LighthouseFriends (after the Civil War) and the nomination (WWI remains); not used. Access: the island is closed per the Boston Harbor Islands site; the bridge closure is from the City of Boston page. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the 1899 Board report (scan page 88, printed page not read) is now cited for the 1900 move; the opening and the 1819/1900 brick-tower dates now say which source gives which date. The Board 1901 lens-change and move entries were checked against the archive text (scan pages 38 and 80).
